meta.phase-name: Escape The Dungeon Asset Authoring Alignment

phase-plan.purpose: Finish the useful Asset Explorer/editor slice quickly, then return to gameplay work. Keep the surface strictly Escape the Dungeon-first: forms/assets for the current game, a clean export/publish round-trip back into the runtime, an Assistant UI chat shell for planning/review/targeted updates inside the hosted product, and a reviewable automated test surface strong enough to keep forms/assets/game/codegen aligned without hand-edit churn. The latest playable/docs-site review and automated test results should also become publicly viewable on GitHub Pages for each main-branch commit.
phase-plan.scope: In scope: direct export/publish workflow, better form/asset management for current game schemas, game-specific widget/binding improvements for awkward authored fields, an optional content-authoring page that unifies forms + assets if the current split feels awkward, a hosted assistant chat bubble built with Assistant UI plus MCP/browser-assistant-friendly contracts, and a testing stack that covers unit, browser UI, deterministic E2E, and reviewable report surfaces. The test/game review surface should publish the latest build artifacts and summaries to GitHub Pages on every main-branch commit so the repo always has a current public review page. Prefer existing user subscriptions where possible; if that is not practical, support OpenRouter-backed models as the default hosted fallback. Out of scope: broad auth tightening, generalized multi-project productization, and diff/review governance.

file.description: Main game-facing asset authoring surface; finish export/publish workflow, forms/assets management, and the hosted assistant handoff here.
Existing content-authoring page may need to be reduced, redirected, or rebuilt around forms/assets plus the BYO assistant shell.
Keep project detail and export/publish helpers aligned with Escape the Dungeon canonical forms, assets, and contract-shaped output.
Likely integration point for MCP/browser-assistant interoperability once the editor exposes toolable operations to the hosted assistant shell.
Probable hosted chat endpoint for Assistant UI if the product uses OpenRouter or another server-mediated model gateway instead of pure client-side subscription handoff.
Unit and browser-oriented Vitest reporting/coverage baseline for reviewable docs-site test output.
Deterministic end-to-end and visual baseline harness for docs-site and game/content editor flows.
Single-page review surface for unit/browser/e2e result summaries so testing stays visible in the product UI and can be mirrored into a public Pages build.
Current CI source of truth for docs-site/game checks and build artifacts; it should become the producer for publishable latest test/game review data.
Static review-site generator that turns the latest game/test artifacts into a GitHub Pages-friendly site bundle with links into the standalone game and HTML reports.
Project export endpoint that should be directly reachable from the new Asset Explorer workflow.
Project publish endpoint for pushing canonical pack edits back into engine/game artifacts.
Top-level route for the Escape the Dungeon-first content authoring loop.

task.description: Finish the direct export/publish workflow and tighten the forms/assets management flow so canonical asset editing stays tied to the playable game loop instead of a separate content page.
Add the first Escape the Dungeon-specific schema/form improvements for awkward authored fields and bindings instead of growing generic schema tooling.

Add a hosted assistant chat shell for Asset Explorer/content authoring using Assistant UI as an expandable bubble, with tool contracts designed for MCP/browser assistants and a model-routing strategy that prefers existing user subscriptions when possible but falls back cleanly to OpenRouter-hosted models.

Document the canonical DB-backed asset loop clearly: supported game schemas seed into Payload, canonical data edits round-trip through export/publish, the assistant shell lives inside the hosted UI, and the game remains the primary consumer.

Close the useful Asset Explorer/editor lane once the game-specific forms/assets + hosted assistant shell are coherent enough, then return active development focus to gameplay/content authored with coding agents.

Stand up the reviewable testing surface for Asset Explorer/game/schema/codegen work: strong unit coverage, browser-mode UI/component tests, deterministic Playwright E2E/visual flows, and a docs-site page that summarizes current results for fast human review.

Reduce alignment churn with concrete mass-update mechanisms instead of relying on AI for routine API drift: shared route clients/types, generated schemas/contracts, codemod-ready helpers, and central test fixtures/report parsers.

Publish the latest docs-site game/test review surface to GitHub Pages on each main-branch commit: promote CI artifacts into page-friendly data, surface latest status/coverage/report links in the docs UI, and keep commit-specific raw artifacts available through Actions for deeper debugging.

decision.summary: Phase 63 should continue only where it improves Escape the Dungeon authoring, inspection, balance, and play-loop support; generic product ambitions stay secondary.
decision.impact: The next editor work is justified only when it helps the real game content pipeline, which keeps the team out of another open-ended tooling detour.

decision.summary: The editor should become a hosted AI product. The chat surface lives in the UI, prefers existing user subscriptions where practical, but must still work when we provide the model path ourselves through OpenRouter or a similar hosted gateway.
decision.impact: This keeps the editor self-contained and usable in-browser while still letting us opportunistically reduce cost/friction with external subscriptions when integrations allow it.

decision.summary: The assistant chat is for planning, review, and targeted updates to forms/assets. Bulk schema/content authoring still remains viable through coding agents working directly in the repo.
decision.impact: The assistant shell stays lightweight and supportive instead of replacing the main development workflow.

decision.summary: The planning snapshot/rollup should eventually treat `deferred` work as closed enough for current-lane progress reporting, or otherwise surface a separate effective-progress metric.
decision.impact: Phase progress will better match reality when non-critical work is intentionally parked instead of continuing to drag the percentage down.

decision.summary: Keep Playwright as the deterministic baseline for end-to-end and visual regression, use Vitest for fast unit coverage plus browser-mode UI/component tests, and treat AI-browser tooling such as Stagehand as optional exploratory assistance for volatile workflows rather than the primary assertion runner.
decision.impact: We keep a stable, debuggable, cost-controlled test pyramid while still leaving room for AI-assisted browser tooling where it saves time instead of introducing flake into the main gate.

decision.summary: For keeping forms/assets/game/codegen aligned, prefer generated route/types/schema clients, shared test fixtures, and codemod-capable helpers over relying on chat agents for repetitive repo-wide API updates.
decision.impact: Mass changes stay cheap, reviewable, and deterministic, with AI helping at the edges instead of becoming the only alignment mechanism.

decision.summary: The public, current review surface for the game/editor/testing stack should live on GitHub Pages and update on every main-branch commit. Actions artifacts remain the deep-dive source for commit-specific logs, HTML reports, and large attachments.
decision.impact: The team can always inspect the latest playable/docs-site state and test health without opening Actions first, while preserving richer per-run artifacts for debugging.
